pu2-ch1.title: 1. Flower Structure & Androecium
pts: Flower → androecium (stamens, male) + gynoecium (pistils, female)
Stamen = filament + anther; anther bilobed & dithecous (2 thecae + connective)
Each theca → 2 microsporangia → 4 microsporangia per anther
Wall layers: epidermis → endothecium → middle layers → tapetum
Tapetum nutrition ↑ → pollen development ↑; sporogenous tissue lies in the centre

pu2-ch1.title: 2. Microsporogenesis & Pollen Grain
pts: PMC (2n) → meiosis → microspore tetrad (4 haploid microspores) → pollen grains
Pollen grain = male gametophyte, 25–50 µm, spherical
Exine (sporopollenin + germ pores) → resistance ↑; intine (cellulose + pectin) thin & continuous
Shed 2-celled (vegetative + generative) or 3-celled in ~60% of angiosperms
Humidity/temperature → viability ↓; liquid N₂ at –196°C → storage ↑ (pollen banks)

pu2-ch1.title: 3. Gynoecium & Megasporogenesis
pts: Gynoecium → monocarpellary or multicarpellary (syncarpous Papaver / apocarpous Michelia)
Pistil = stigma → style → ovary (locule + placenta + ovules)
Ovule: funicle → hilum → integuments → micropyle; chalaza at the opposite base
Nucellus (reserve food) → encloses the embryo sac
MMC (2n) → meiosis → dyad → tetrad of 4 haploid megaspores

pu2-ch1.title: 4. Female Gametophyte Development
pts: 4 megaspores → 1 functional, 3 degenerate → monosporic development
Free-nuclear mitoses: 2-nucleate → 4-nucleate → 8-nucleate embryo sac
Cellularisation → 6 nuclei walled off, 2 polar nuclei stay in the central cell
Micropylar end → egg apparatus (2 synergids + 1 egg); filiform apparatus guides the pollen tube
Chalazal end → 3 antipodals; mature sac = 7-celled, 8-nucleate

pu2-ch1.title: 5. Pollination
pts: Anther → stigma: autogamy (same flower) → geitonogamy (same plant) → xenogamy (different plant, genetic variation ↑)
Cleistogamous flowers never open (Viola, Oxalis, Commelina) → assured seed set ↑ but variation ↓
Wind: feathery stigma + light non-sticky pollen → corn cob tassels; Water: Vallisneria, Hydrilla, Zostera (ribbon-like pollen)
Animals: colour + scent + nectar → bees, bats, birds; Yucca–moth = obligate mutualism; pollen/nectar robbers give nothing back
Selfing → inbreeding depression ↑ → outbreeding devices: self-incompatibility, asynchrony, monoecy (autogamy ↓) and dioecy in papaya (both ↓)

pu2-ch1.title: 6. Pollen-Pistil Interaction & Artificial Hybridisation
pts: Pollen lands → pistil recognises chemically → right type accepted, wrong type inhibited
Germination → stigma → style → ovary → micropyle → filiform apparatus → synergid
2-celled pollen: generative cell divides in the tube; 3-celled pollen: 2 male gametes carried from the start
Artificial hybridisation → emasculate the bud (before dehiscence) → bag → dust desired pollen on receptive stigma → re-bag
Unisexual female parent → emasculation not needed → bud directly bagged; contamination ↓, purity of cross ↑

pu2-ch1.title: 7. Double Fertilisation & Post-fertilisation Development
pts: Pollen tube bursts in a synergid → 2 male gametes released
Gamete 1 + egg = syngamy → zygote (2n); gamete 2 + 2 polar nuclei = triple fusion → PEN (3n)
Two fusions in one embryo sac = double fertilisation, unique to angiosperms; synergids & antipodals degenerate
Endosperm first → free-nuclear (coconut water) → cellular (white kernel); zygote divides only after food supply ↑
Zygote → pro-embryo → globular → heart-shaped → mature embryo; dicot = epicotyl/hypocotyl, monocot = scutellum + coleoptile + coleorrhiza

pu2-ch1.title: 8. Seed & Fruit Development, Apomixis & Polyembryony
pts: Ovule → seed (seed coat + cotyledons + embryonal axis); ovary → fruit (pericarp)
Endosperm persists → albuminous (wheat, maize, castor); endosperm used up → non-albuminous (pea, groundnut); nucellus persists → perisperm (black pepper, beet)
Moisture ↓ → dormancy → viability ↑: Lupinus arcticus 10,000 yr, Phoenix dactylifera ~2,000 yr
Ovary only → true fruit (mango, tomato); thalamus also → false fruit (apple, strawberry); no fertilisation → parthenocarpy (banana, seedless)
Apomixis = seed without fertilisation → clonal progeny → hybrid vigour retained, seed cost ↓; nucellar polyembryony in Citrus & mango

pu2-ch2.title: 1. Male Reproductive System
pts: Testes in scrotum → temp ↓ by 2–2.5°C → spermatogenesis possible
Testis → ~250 lobules → 1–3 seminiferous tubules (spermatogonia + Sertoli cells)
Leydig cells outside tubules → androgens (testosterone) ↑
Ducts: rete testis → vasa efferentia → epididymis → vas deferens → ejaculatory duct → urethra
Glands (2 seminal vesicles + 1 prostate + 2 bulbourethral) → alkaline seminal plasma (fructose, Ca, enzymes) = 60% of semen

pu2-ch2.title: 2. Female Reproductive System
pts: Ovary (2–4 cm) → ovum + steroid hormones; stroma = cortex + medulla
Oviduct (10–12 cm): infundibulum + fimbriae → ampulla → isthmus → uterus
Uterus wall: perimetrium → myometrium (labour contractions ↑) → endometrium (cyclic changes)
Cervical canal + vagina = birth canal; hymen is NOT a test of virginity
Breast: 15–20 lobes → alveoli → tubules → duct → ampulla → lactiferous duct; prolactin = secretion, oxytocin = ejection

pu2-ch2.title: 3. Gametogenesis
pts: Spermatogonium (2n) → primary spermatocyte → 2 secondary spermatocytes (n) → 4 spermatids → 4 sperms
Spermiogenesis (spermatid → sperm) → spermiation (release into tubule lumen)
GnRH ↑ → LH/ICSH → Leydig cells → testosterone ↑; FSH → Sertoli cells → spermiogenesis
Sperm: acrosome (enzymes) + haploid nucleus → head; mitochondria → middle piece → energy for tail
Oogenesis starts in foetal life → primary oocyte (arrested prophase-I) → 60,000–80,000 at puberty → Graafian follicle → ovulation

pu2-ch2.title: 4. Menstrual Cycle
pts: Menarche (12–15 yrs) → cycles of 28–29 days → menopause (~50 yrs); primates only.
Menstrual (3–5 d) → Follicular → Ovulatory → Luteal.
FSH ↑ → follicle grows → oestrogen ↑ → endometrium regenerates.
Day 14: LH surge → Graafian follicle ruptures → ovulation.
Corpus luteum → progesterone ↑ → endometrium maintained; no fertilisation → luteum degenerates → progesterone ↓ → menstruation.

pu2-ch2.title: 5. Fertilisation & Early Embryonic Development
pts: Insemination → sperms through cervix & uterus → ampullary–isthmic junction = site of fertilisation.
Acrosomal enzymes → sperm enters; zona pellucida changes → polyspermy blocked (only ONE sperm).
Sperm entry → meiosis-II completed → ovum + 2nd polar body → nuclei fuse → diploid zygote.
Cleavage in isthmus: 2 → 4 → 8 → 16 blastomeres → morula (8–16 cells) → blastocyst.
Blastocyst = trophoblast + inner cell mass → implantation → pregnancy; XX/XY decided by father's sperm.

pu2-ch2.title: 6. Pregnancy, Parturition & Lactation
pts: Trophoblast → chorionic villi + uterine tissue → placenta (umbilical cord links foetus).
Placenta: O₂ & nutrients in ↑, CO₂ & wastes out; endocrine → hCG, hPL, oestrogens, progestogens, relaxin.
Gastrulation → ectoderm + mesoderm + endoderm → all tissues & organs.
1 month heart → 2 months limbs/digits → 12 weeks organs → 5th month movements & hair → 9 months full term.
Foetal ejection reflex → oxytocin ↑ → stronger contractions → more oxytocin (positive feedback) → birth; then prolactin (milk secretion) + oxytocin (ejection), colostrum → immunity.

pu2-ch3.title: 1. Reproductive Health & RCH Programme
pts: WHO: reproductive health = total wellbeing → physical + emotional + behavioural + social
India first to act → family planning 1951 → broadened into RCH programmes
RCH aims: awareness → sex education → birth control → pre/post-natal care → STD awareness → rural medical help
Statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination → female foeticide ↓
Saheli (CDRI Lucknow) → non-steroidal once-a-week pill; success shown by MMR ↓, IMR ↓, STDs ↓

pu2-ch3.title: 2. Population Explosion & Birth Control Overview
pts: World 2 billion (1900) → 6 billion (2000); India 350 million (1947) → 1 billion (May 2000)
Cause: death rate ↓ (MMR ↓, IMR ↓) + people of reproducible age ↑
Steps: marriageable age ↑ (18 F / 21 M) → incentives for small families → “HUM DO HAMARE DO”
Ideal contraceptive → user-friendly + available + effective & reversible + no side effects + libido unaffected
Methods split → Natural (avoid meeting of gametes) vs Artificial (barriers, IUDs, pills, surgical)

pu2-ch3.title: 3. Natural & Barrier Contraceptive Methods
pts: Natural principle → avoid the chance meeting of ovum and sperm; no device, no side effects, failure ↑
Rhythm method → avoid coitus day 10 – day 17 (fertile period, ovulation expected)
Coitus interruptus → withdrawal just before ejaculation; LAM → works only up to 6 months after parturition
Condoms (Nirodh) → thin latex, disposable, self-inserted, privacy + protection from STDs & AIDS
Diaphragm / cervical cap / vault → reusable, cover cervix; + spermicides → efficiency ↑

pu2-ch3.title: 4. IUDs & Hormonal Contraceptives
pts: All IUDs → phagocytosis of sperms ↑ in uterus; ideal to delay pregnancy / space children
Lippes loop → sterile inflammatory response; CuT / Cu7 / Multiload 375 → Cu ions → sperm motility ↓
Progestasert / LNG-20 → uterus unsuitable for implantation + cervix hostile to sperms
Pills (progesterone ± oestrogen) → ovulation ↓ + implantation ↓ + cervical mucus altered; 21 days on → 7 days gap
Depo Provera (injection), Implanon / Norplant (implants) → longer action; emergency contraception within 72 hours

pu2-ch3.title: 5. Surgical Methods & Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP)
pts: Vasectomy → ties/removes vas deferens → blocks sperm
Tubectomy → ties/removes fallopian tube → blocks ova
MTP legalised in India in 1971 with strict conditions
1st trimester = safer ↓ risk; 2nd trimester = ↑ risk
Unhealthy trend: illegal MTPs + amniocentesis misuse → female foeticide

pu2-ch3.title: 6. Sexually Transmitted Diseases (STDs/STIs)
pts: Spread mainly via unsafe coitus; Hep-B/HIV also via needles, blood, mother→foetus
Curable: all except Hepatitis-B, Herpes, HIV
Early symptoms mild ↓ often missed, esp. in females
Untreated → PID, ectopic pregnancy, infertility, cancer
Prevention: avoid multiple partners ↑ use condoms ↑ early treatment

pu2-ch3.title: 7. Infertility
pts: Definition: no conception after ∼2 years of unprotected intercourse
Male causes → impotency, cryptorchidism, oligo/azoo/astheno-spermia
Female causes → hormonal imbalance, blocked tube, uterine/vaginal defects
Normal sperm count 50–150 million/ml; oligospermia <20 million/ml
Fertility clinics diagnose → ART offers treatment

pu2-ch3.title: 8. Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART)
pts: IVF = fertilisation outside body → 'test tube baby'
ZIFT: ≤8 blastomeres → fallopian tube | IUT: >8 blastomeres → uterus
GIFT: donor ovum + sperm → recipient's fallopian tube (fertilisation in vivo)
ICSI: sperm injected directly into ovum cytoplasm
AI: semen introduced into vagina/uterus → treats male-factor infertility

pu2-ch5.title: 1 · DNA STRUCTURE
pts: Nucleoside (base+sugar, N-glycosidic) → Nucleotide (+phosphate) → 3′-5′ phosphodiester chain
Meischer · Wilkins & Franklin · Watson & Crick · Chargaff
Antiparallel · A=T (2 H-bonds), G≡C (3) · right-handed
Pitch 3.4 nm · 10 bp/turn · 0.34 nm · 20 Å
Central dogma; reverse transcription (Temin & Baltimore, 1970)

pu2-ch5.title: 2 · PACKAGING
pts: 6.6 × 109 bp × 0.34 nm = 2.2 m in a 10−6 m nucleus
Prokaryote: nucleoid, loops, basic non-histone proteins
Eukaryote: histone octamer (lysine, arginine) → nucleosome (~200 bp)
Beads-on-string → chromatin fibre (NHC) → chromosome
Euchromatin (active) vs heterochromatin (inactive)

pu2-ch5.title: 3 · SEARCH FOR GENETIC MATERIAL
pts: Griffith 1928 → transforming principle (S vs R strain)
Avery, MacLeod & McCarty → DNase abolishes transformation
Hershey & Chase 1952 → <sup>32</sup>P in, <sup>35</sup>S out
Properties: replicate · stable · mutable · expressible
DNA vs RNA; RNA evolved first (TMV, Qβ)

pu2-ch5.title: 4 · REPLICATION
pts: Semi-conservative (Watson & Crick 1953), S phase
Meselson & Stahl 1958: <sup>15</sup>N, CsCl gradient, hybrid → hybrid+light
Taylor 1958: Vicia faba, radioactive thymidine
Origin · fork · 5′→3′ only · leading vs lagging
Okazaki fragments + ligase · ~2000 bp/sec in E. coli

pu2-ch5.title: 5 · TRANSCRIPTION
pts: Promoter – structural gene – terminator
Template (3′→5′) vs coding strand (misnomer)
Cistron · monocistronic/split vs polycistronic · exon/intron
mRNA, tRNA, rRNA · sigma (start), rho (stop)
Pol I / II / III · capping, tailing, splicing

pu2-ch5.title: 6 · GENETIC CODE & tRNA
pts: Gamow 4<sup>3</sup> = 64 · Khorana, Nirenberg, Ochoa
Triplet · unambiguous · degenerate · universal · commaless
AUG start/Met · UAA, UAG, UGA stop
Exceptions: ciliates, human mitochondria
Point (sickle-cell) vs frameshift · tRNA = adaptor

pu2-ch5.title: 7 · TRANSLATION & REGULATION
pts: Activation → charging → initiation → elongation → termination
23S rRNA = ribozyme · translational unit & UTRs
Operon = polycistronic + promoter + regulatory genes
Lac (inducible, catabolic): i, p, o, z, y, a – Jacob & Monod 1961
Trp (repressible, anabolic): aporepressor + tryptophan corepressor

pu2-ch5.title: 8 · HGP & DNA FINGERPRINTING
pts: 1990–2003 · DOE + NIH + Wellcome Trust · ELSI
ESTs vs sequence annotation · BAC/YAC · Sanger
3 × 10<sup>9</sup> bases · ~30,000 genes · <2% coding
Dystrophin 2.4 Mb · chr 1 = 2968, Y = 231 · SNPs 1.4 million
Jeffreys · VNTR · digest → electrophoresis → Southern blot → autoradiography

pu2-ch6.title: 1 · ORIGIN OF UNIVERSE & EARTH
pts: Big Bang (Lemaitre, 1927) · ~15 billion years ago
Nebular theory (Kant, 1755) · earth ~4.5 billion years old
Early atmosphere: H<sub>2</sub>O, CH<sub>4</sub>, CO<sub>2</sub>, NH<sub>3</sub>
UV split water → O<sub>2</sub> escaped · ozone layer formed
Life appeared ~500 million years after earth formed (~4 bya)

pu2-ch6.title: 2 · THEORIES OF ORIGIN OF LIFE
pts: Special Creation (Father Suarez) · Cosmozoic/Panspermia (Richter)
Abiogenesis (Aristotle, spontaneous generation)
Biogenesis (Redi 1688 → Spallanzani 1765 → Pasteur, swan-neck flask)
Pasteur disproved abiogenesis once and for all

pu2-ch6.title: 3 · CHEMICAL EVOLUTION OF LIFE
pts: Oparin (1924) & Haldane · reducing atmosphere
Inorganic → simple organic → macromolecules → protobiont
Coacervates (Oparin, 1938) · Microspheres (Sydney Fox, 1959)
Miller-Urey (1953): CH<sub>4</sub>:NH<sub>3</sub>:H<sub>2</sub> = 2:1:2, spark discharge → amino acids

pu2-ch6.title: 4 · EVIDENCES OF EVOLUTION
pts: Paleontological (fossils, radioactive dating)
Embryological (biogenetic law – Haeckel; disproved by von Baer)
Morphological: homologous (divergent) vs analogous (convergent)
Biochemical (proteins, genes) · Biogeographical (finches, marsupials)
Natural selection in action: adaptive/industrial melanism

pu2-ch6.title: 5 · LAMARCKISM
pts: Jean Baptist Lamarck, Philosophie Zoologique (1809)
Use & disuse of organs · inheritance of acquired characters
Giraffe neck (use) · snake limblessness (disuse)
Disproved: Weismann's decaudalisation (22 generations)
Germplasm theory (Weismann): somatoplasm vs germplasm

pu2-ch6.title: 6 · DARWINISM & NATURAL SELECTION
pts: Darwin + Wallace · H.M.S. Beagle · Origin of Species (1859)
Overproduction → struggle → variation → survival of fittest (Spencer)
Malthus's population essay influenced Darwin
Types: stabilizing, directional, disruptive selection
Criticism: doesn't explain vestigial organs, arrival of fittest

pu2-ch6.title: 7 · MUTATION THEORY & HARDY-WEINBERG
pts: Hugo de Vries (1901) · Oenothera lamarckiana · saltation
Mutation: large, random, sudden vs Darwinian: small, directional
H-W: p + q = 1, p<sup>2</sup>+2pq+q<sup>2</sup>=1 (genetic equilibrium)
Disturbed by: migration, drift, mutation, recombination, selection
Founder effect = bottleneck / Sewall Wright effect

pu2-ch6.title: 8 · ORIGIN & EVOLUTION OF MAN
pts: Dryopithecus & Ramapithecus (~15 mya)
Australopithecus (~2 mya, 500–700cc, Lucy)
Homo habilis (650–800cc) → Homo erectus (~900cc, Java/Peking man)
Homo neanderthalensis (1400cc) → Homo sapiens (modern man)
Cro-Magnon man – most recent direct ancestor

pu2-ch7.title: 1. Health & Disease
pts: WHO: complete physical, mental & social well-being
Causes: genetic, infections, lifestyle

pu2-ch7.title: 2. Bacterial & Viral Diseases
pts: Typhoid — Salmonella typhi (small intestine)
Pneumonia — S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae (alveoli)
Common cold — Rhinovirus (upper respiratory tract)

pu2-ch7.title: 3. Protozoan, Fungal & Helminthic
pts: Malaria — Plasmodium (Anopheles vector)
Amoebiasis — Entamoeba histolytica (housefly)
Ascariasis, Elephantiasis, Ringworm

pu2-ch7.title: 4. Prevention & Control
pts: Personal & public hygiene
Vector control (Gambusia fish, nets)
Vaccination programmes

pu2-ch7.title: 5. Innate Immunity
pts: Physical, physiological, cellular, cytokine barriers
Non-specific, present from birth

pu2-ch7.title: 6. Acquired Immunity & Vaccination
pts: Primary vs secondary response
Antibody H2L2 structure
Active vs passive immunity
Vaccination = immunological memory

pu2-ch7.title: 7. Immune Disorders & Lymphoid Organs
pts: Allergies, autoimmunity
Primary: bone marrow, thymus
Secondary: spleen, lymph nodes, tonsils, MALT

pu2-ch7.title: 8. AIDS
pts: HIV — retrovirus
Macrophage → helper T-cell replication
ELISA (screening) → Western blot (confirm)

pu2-ch7.title: 9. Cancer
pts: Benign vs malignant, metastasis
Biopsy, CT, MRI
Surgery, radiotherapy, chemotherapy, immunotherapy

pu2-ch7.title: 10. Drugs & Alcohol Abuse
pts: Opioids, cannabinoids, coca alkaloids
Tolerance, dependence, withdrawal
Prevention in adolescents

pu2-ch8.title: 1. Microbes in Household Products
pts: Curd: LAB / Lactobacillus → acid coagulates milk protein; ↑ vitamin B12
Starter curd = inoculum of thousands of LAB; LAB check gut pathogens
Idli & dosa: bacteria → CO2 → puffed-up dough
Bread: Saccharomyces cerevisiae (baker's yeast); Toddy: fermented palm sap
Cheese: Swiss holes = CO2 by Propionibacterium sharmanii; Roquefort ripened by a fungus

pu2-ch8.title: 2. Industrial Products
pts: Fermentors = large vessels for industrial scale-up
Beverages: brewer's yeast; wine/beer undistilled, whisky/rum distilled
Penicillin: Fleming + Chain + Florey, Nobel 1945
Acids: Aspergillus (citric), Acetobacter (acetic), Clostridium (butyric)
Enzymes/bioactive: lipase, pectinase-protease, streptokinase, cyclosporin A, statins

pu2-ch8.title: 3. Sewage Treatment
pts: Primary = physical: filtration + sedimentation → primary sludge + effluent
Secondary = biological: aeration tank → flocs → BOD reduced
BOD = O₂ needed to oxidise organic matter in 1 L water; high BOD = more polluting
Activated sludge: part as inoculum, rest to anaerobic digesters → biogas
Ganga & Yamuna Action Plans – Ministry of Environment and Forests

pu2-ch8.title: 4. Biogas
pts: Biogas = mixture of gases, mainly methane; used as fuel
Methanogens (Methanobacterium): anaerobic, on cellulose → CH4 + CO2 + H2
Present in rumen of cattle → dung (gobar) rich in them → gobar gas
Plant: 10-15 ft concrete tank + dung slurry, floating cover, gas outlet pipe, sludge outlet
IARI & KVIC; used for cooking & lighting; spent slurry = fertiliser

pu2-ch8.title: 5. Microbes as Biocontrol Agents
pts: Chemicals: non-selective, toxic, distort food chains
Ladybird → aphids; Dragonfly → mosquitoes
Bt spores in sachets → kill butterfly caterpillars
Bt gene in plant = Bt-cotton (genetic engineering)
Trichoderma → plant pathogens; Nucleopolyhedrovirus → narrow spectrum; used in IPM

pu2-ch8.title: 6. Microbes as Biofertilizers
pts: Biofertilizers = organisms enriching soil nutrients (replace polluting chemical fertilizers)
Bacteria: Rhizobium in legume root nodules → fixes atmospheric nitrogen
Fungi: Glomus → mycorrhiza → absorbs phosphorus for the plant
Cyanobacteria: Nostoc, Anabaena → fix nitrogen, mainly in paddy fields
Closing idea: microbes are diverse & largely beneficial, not merely pathogenic

pu2-ch10.title: 1. GM Crops & Bt Cotton
pts: 3 routes to more food → agro-chemical, organic, GM crop-based
GM crops ↑ stress tolerance, pest resistance, nutrition (Golden Rice = Vit A)
B. thuringiensis crystal = inactive protoxin
Alkaline insect gut pH → activates toxin → binds midgut cells → pores → cell lysis ↓
cry genes (IAc, IIAb, IAb) inserted → Bt cotton, corn, rice, tomato, potato, soyabean

pu2-ch10.title: 2. RNA Interference (RNAi)
pts: Complementary RNA + target mRNA → dsRNA → translation blocked ↓
Natural defence in eukaryotic cells vs RNA viruses & transposons
Used against nematode Meloidegyne incognitia in tobacco roots
Agrobacterium vector → nematode gene inserted, transcribed both directions
Sense + anti-sense RNA anneal → dsRNA → silences nematode mRNA → parasite can't survive

pu2-ch10.title: 3. Recombinant Insulin & Gene Therapy
pts: Animal insulin → allergic reactions; pro-insulin = A+B+C chains, mature = A+B only
Eli Lilly 1983: A & B chain genes → separate E. coli plasmids → joined by disulphide bonds
Gene therapy = deliver normal gene to fix defective gene
1990 ADA deficiency: first clinical gene therapy, age 4 girl
Lymphocytes + retroviral vector + ADA cDNA → reinfused; not permanent (cells die) ↓ needs periodic repeats

pu2-ch10.title: 4. Molecular Diagnosis
pts: Early diagnosis hard when pathogen conc. is ↓ and no symptoms yet
PCR → amplifies target DNA ↑-fold → detects HIV, cancer gene mutations
ELISA → antigen-antibody interaction → detects pathogen antigen OR patient antibody
Radioactive probe hybridises with patient DNA → autoradiography
Mutation site → probe can't bind → gap/no signal on autoradiograph film

pu2-ch10.title: 5. Transgenic Animals
pts: Animal + extra foreign gene (transgene) = transgenic; 95%+ are mice
Model normal physiology/development → gene regulation insights
Disease models: cancer, cystic fibrosis, rheumatoid arthritis, Alzheimer's
Biological products in milk: alpha-1-antitrypsin, Rosie the cow (1997) → alpha-lactalbumin
Vaccine safety (polio) & toxicity testing ↑ sensitivity, faster results

pu2-ch10.title: 6. Ethical Issues, GEAC & Biopiracy
pts: GEAC = India's GM regulatory/approval body
Ethical concerns → animal welfare & ecological risk of GMO release
Patent disputes → 1997 Basmati rice, Neem, turmeric claimed by MNCs
Biopiracy = bio-resource/knowledge use without authorisation or fair compensation
Developed (biodiv-poor, $ rich) exploits developing (biodiv-rich) → 2nd amendment to Patents Bill

pu2-ch11.title: 1. Organisms and Their Environment
pts: Ecology → organisms → populations → communities → biomes
Earth’s rotation → seasons → biomes (desert, grassland, forest, tundra); India: rain forest, deciduous forest, desert, sea coast
Temperature = most relevant abiotic factor → stenothermal (narrow) vs eurythermal (wide)
Water: quantity limits on land, quality (salinity, ppt) limits in oceans → stenohaline vs euryhaline
Soil (composition, grain size, percolation, water holding capacity) + Light (photosynthesis, photoperiodism; land ↑ water ↓)

pu2-ch11.title: 2. Responses to Stress & Adaptations
pts: Homeostasis → 4 strategies: Regulate → Conform → Migrate → Suspend
Regulators (birds, mammals) hold 37°C — sweat ↓ heat, shiver ↑ heat; conformers follow ambient because regulation costs ↑ energy
Migrate = escape in space (birds); Suspend = escape in time → spores, hibernation, aestivation, diapause
Desert plants: thick cuticle + sunken stomata + CAM (stomata closed by day) + spines → flattened stems photosynthesise
Cold → Allen’s rule (short limbs/ears), fur, blubber; High altitude → ↑RBC, ↓Hb binding, ↑breathing; Desert animals → burrow, fat oxidation, concentrated urine

pu2-ch11.title: 3. Population Attributes
pts: Population = similar individuals + one area + shared resources + interbreeding
Attributes an individual lacks → birth rate, death rate, sex ratio, age distribution, density
Birth rate & death rate = per 1000 people per year (per capita)
Age pyramid: triangular → expanding ↑; bell → stable; urn → declining ↓
Population density (N) = individuals per niche → huge population? use relative density, not absolute

pu2-ch11.title: 4. Population Growth
pts: Density ↑ by Natality (B) + Immigration (I); density ↓ by Mortality (D) + Emigration (E) → N(t+1) = N(t) + [(B+I) – (D+E)]
Unlimited resources → Exponential growth → dN/dt = rN → Nt = N0ert → J-shaped curve
Limited resources → competition → Logistic growth → dN/dt = rN(K–N)/K → sigmoid Verhulst–Pearl curve
Lag → acceleration → deceleration → asymptote at K; N → K makes dN/dt ↓ to zero
r ↑ = Darwinian fitness ↑: breed once (salmon, bamboo) vs many times (birds, mammals); many small (oysters) vs few large (mammals) offspring

pu2-ch11.title: 5. Population Interactions I — Predation and Competition
pts: Predation (+/–) → energy transfer to the next higher trophic level → ecosystem balance maintained
Plants vs herbivores → thorns, secondary metabolites, poisonous chemicals
Animals vs predators → camouflage; Monarch butterfly distasteful ← chemical acquired as caterpillar from a poisonous weed
Competition (–/–) → closely related species, same habitat + food → fitness ↓ → survival of the fittest
Gause's principle → inferior competitor eliminated; unless co-existence mechanisms evolve → both survive

pu2-ch11.title: 6. Population Interactions II — Parasitism, Commensalism, Mutualism
pts: Parasitism (+/–) → hooks & suckers, digestive system lost, reproduction ↑; ecto (lice, ticks, Cuscuta) vs endo (Plasmodium, tapeworm)
Brood parasitism → Koel egg → crow's nest → host rears the parasite's chick
Commensalism (+/0) → orchid on mango, barnacle on whale, cattle egret ← insects flushed out, clown fish ← anemone's stinging tentacles
Mutualism (+/+) → lichen (fungus support + alga food), mycorrhiza (fungus nutrients + plant carbohydrates)
Fig ↔ wasp one-to-one and Ophrys sexual deceit → co-evolution; table: ++ Mutualism, –– Competition, +– Predation/Parasitism, +0 Commensalism, –0 Amensalism

pu2-ch12.title: 1. Structure of Ecosystem
pts: Ecosystem = living things ↔ each other ↔ surrounding environment
Two basic types → terrestrial (forest, grassland, desert) & aquatic (pond, lake, river, ocean)
Biotic × abiotic interactions → maintenance of the ecosystem
Stratification = vertical distribution → trees above shrubs above herbs
Four functional aspects → productivity, decomposition, energy flow, nutrient cycling

pu2-ch12.title: 2. Productivity
pts: Constant sunlight → proper functioning of every ecosystem
Primary productivity = biomass per unit area per unit time by plants → g m⁻² or kcal m⁻²
Depends on plant species + photosynthetic capacity + nutrient availability
GPP − R = NPP → R ↑ means NPP ↓; NPP is what consumers get
Biosphere NPP ≈ 170 b tons/yr; secondary productivity = new organic matter by consumers

pu2-ch12.title: 3. Decomposition
pts: Complex organic matter → inorganic substances (CO₂, water, nutrients)
Detritus → Fragmentation (detritivores) → surface area ↑
Leaching → inorganic matter enters soil (physical); Catabolism → bacterial & fungal enzymes
Humification → humus: resistant, slow, reservoir of nutrients
Mineralization → minerals released into soil; O₂-consuming, detritus chemistry + climate control it

pu2-ch12.title: 4. Energy Flow
pts: Sun = sole energy source → PAR < 50% of solar radiation → only ~1% fixed as NPP
Plants = producers → animals = consumers/heterotrophs (primary → secondary → tertiary)
Food chain = linear energy flow → food web = interconnected food chains → ↑ stability
Trophic level = functional level; standing crop = living material present at that level at a given time
10 percent law → energy ↓ tenfold each step → trophic levels limited to 4–5

pu2-ch12.title: 5. Ecological Pyramids
pts: Pyramid = energy relationship of trophic levels → base = producers, apex = top consumer
3 types → number, biomass, energy
Grassland numbers: 58,42,000 → 7,08,000 → 3,54,000 → only 3 top carnivores
Inverted cases → ocean biomass (phytoplankton 4 ↑ zooplankton 21); number (one tree → many insects)
Energy pyramid ALWAYS upright → limitations: multi-level species, no food webs, saprophytes excluded

pu2-ch13.title: 1. Levels & Patterns of Biodiversity
pts: Edward Wilson → biodiversity = diversity at ALL levels: genetic → species → ecological
Genes: E. coli 4000 → Drosophila 13,000 → human 30,000–40,000; India 50,000+ rice strains
IUCN 1.5 million recorded · 70% insects · Robert May's estimate ↑ to ~7 million
India: 2.4% land but 8.1% species → one of 12 mega diversity countries
Equator → poles: diversity ↓; area ↑ → species ↑ as log S = log C + Z log A

pu2-ch13.title: 2. Importance of Biodiversity
pts: Species diversity → stability + productivity + ecosystem health
More species → resistance & resilience ↑ → year-to-year variation ↓
Diversity ↑ → productivity ↑ (Tilman's plots; tropical forests)
No species lives alone → interactions → ecosystem health → human survival
Ehrlich's rivet popper: ecosystem = airplane, species = rivets; wing rivets (key species) → risk ↑↑

pu2-ch13.title: 3. Loss of Biodiversity
pts: IUCN Red List: 784 species lost in 500 yrs → 338 vertebrates + 359 invertebrates + 87 plants; 27 in last 20 yrs
Habitat loss & fragmentation = MAJOR cause → Amazon 14% → <6%
Over-exploitation → Steller's sea cow, passenger pigeon, Dodo, Quagga, Thylacine, 3 tiger subspecies
Alien invasion → Nile perch in Lake Victoria → 200+ cichlids extinct; Parthenium, Lantana, Eichhornia, Clarias gariepinus
Co-extinction → obligatory partner also lost (plant → pollinator mutualism)

pu2-ch13.title: 4. Why Conserve Biodiversity
pts: Three arguments → narrow utilitarian, broadly utilitarian, ethical
Narrow → food, firewood, fibre, construction material, industrial products, ~25,000 medicinal plants
Broad → Amazon gives 20% of Earth’s O₂; pollination by butterflies, bees, bumblebees, birds, bats
Broad also → flood & erosion control, nutrient replenishment, waste recycling, aesthetic pleasure
Ethical → every species has intrinsic value; biological legacy passed on to future generations

pu2-ch13.title: 5. In-Situ Conservation
pts: In-situ = protection in the natural habitat → whole ecosystem saved
Hotspot = high species richness + high endemism → also accelerated habitat loss
34 hotspots world → 3 in India: Western Ghats & Sri Lanka, Indo-Myanmar, Eastern Himalaya
Hotspots <2% of land → strict protection → mass extinctions ↓ by ~30%
Protected areas → 14 (18) biosphere reserves, 90 (103) national parks, 448 (515) sanctuaries; sacred groves → Meghalaya, Karnataka, Maharashtra, MP, Rajasthan

pu2-ch13.title: 6. Ex-Situ Conservation & Global Efforts
pts: Ex-situ = species taken out of habitat → zoos, botanical gardens, wildlife safari parks
Cryopreservation → gametes viable & fertile at very low temperature
IVF → preserved sperm + egg in vitro → embryo implanted in female; tissue culture → plants
Seed bank → seeds of genetic strains; gene bank → DNA/RNA sequence database
Rio de Janeiro 1992 Earth Summit → Johannesburg 2002, 190 countries pledge biodiversity loss ↓ by 2010
